objective: Prove the dual-pair identity for line contradictions where the exact counts support it, by moving a seam as the two-literal wall does, or explain from the counts and the structure of three-place contradictions why the identity fails.
status: Proved by TRIPLE-SHIELD-20261023-001B-P001 (V1 prose proof; standard-library check of the gauge construction on 210 fitting cases, of 1091 orientation-world configurations with every cylinder certified by its own two-literal solver, and of the exhaustive 3 x 3 line-event counts; three controls rejected). In tiling worlds a cylinder along a class contradicts only in twists odd on it relative to every fitting twist. In the four orientation worlds, where each fair coin decides one clause on two places, a lone line along c is exactly the line event of the shielding theorem, since a contradiction whose cluster has rank two makes every cylinder along an odd class contradict; so dual pairs are equal on every torus. From the frozen exact counts, the identity fails for every tested dual pair of worlds where one coin decides three places (36 three-place and 18 shared-coin pairs on the fresh 3 x 4 and 4 x 4 tori), so the dual-pair identity separates coins that reach two places from coins that reach three, not clause width.
title: Proof: the three-place wall, or why there is none
